A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same budget-allocation study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and section moves.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian simulations, MNIST denoising results, and Llama-3 math-reasoning experiments, including parameter and temperature analyses in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds mixed-policy math-reasoning results in Appendix F.5 and Table 3.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and the original allocation policies remain unchanged. Appendix F.5 adds an evaluated mixed policy that starts with linear growth and switches to exponential growth when improvement stalls, a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Gaussian simulations, MNIST denoising with the same CIFAR-10-pretrained diffusion model, and GSM_symbolic, GSM_p1, and GSM_p2 reasoning. The mixed-policy experiment uses existing tasks; the Gaussian experiment is reorganized rather than removed.

E2.justification: The original pretrained, constant, linear, and exponential comparisons are retained. v2 adds the mixed schedule as a comparator against linear and exponential policies in Appendix F.5 and Table 3.

E3.justification: Denoising settings change from s = 0.01/0.02 to s = 10/20, while the plotted curves and performance values remain identical. The appendix still defines normalized diffusion time without specifying the conversion, so a notation change cannot reliably be distinguished from a protocol revision. Other established hyperparameters and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F.5 adds an analysis of whether switching from linear to exponential allocation improves math reasoning. The Gaussian parameter studies, exponential-policy ablations, and temperature comparison in Appendices F.1–F.4 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging Gaussian results over 1,000 runs in Figure 2. v2 introduces no new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation practice; its mixed-policy table reports point estimates.

E6.justification: The original performance tables retain their values in v2 Table 2. New Table 3 reports mixed-policy accuracies of 65.98, 45.56, and 20.16 on symbolic/p1/p2, versus exponential scores of 65.66, 47.26, and 20.65. v2 also newly reports noisy-input PSNR values of 33.25 and 28.40.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.5 defines an additive reward perturbation with zero-mean noise independent of R(x) and briefly argues that the theoretical conclusions extend to this setting. The central Gaussian and general-policy theorems and their proofs are otherwise substantively retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about constant-policy nonconvergence, increasing-policy convergence, and exponential allocation's optimality or efficiency advantages. The more explicit supervised-fine-tuning wording reflects a scope already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability qualifications: oracle-reward denoising is explicitly framed as theoretical validation, and Appendix G discusses biased rewards, reward hacking, production-scale limitations, and degradation under prolonged fine-tuning. It also adds explanations of allocation timing and clarifies the distinction between asymptotic convergence and budget-constrained comparisons.

D1.justification: v2 replaces separate image and math code references with a unified repository reference covering all experiments. Appendices E.3–E.4 newly disclose NVIDIA A800 hardware and approximately 100 and 400 GPU-hours per denoising and reasoning configuration, respectively. Existing hyperparameters are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning verification/correction, VLM applications, and SFT's relationship to RL, including Gillman et al., El Firdoussi et al., Gandhi et al., and DeepSeek-R1. Some introductory citations are removed, but the central finite-sample positioning relative to Ferbach et al. remains.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the exposition by separating general theory into Section 4, integrating Gaussian results into Section 3.2, moving their detailed setup to Appendix E.2, swapping Appendices C/D, and relocating the impact statement into Appendix G. The introduction and denoising discussion are also substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive figure and algorithm repositioning and rescaling. Table 1 is redesigned, v1 Tables 2–3 become paired panels of v2 Table 2, and a new mixed-policy Table 3 is added. Existing plots are retained rather than replaced with new results.

improvement.justification: Explicit oracle-reward and biased-reward limitations, hardware/runtime disclosures, consolidated code instructions, and the mixed-policy comparison modestly improve transparency and usefulness. Core empirical support remains largely unchanged. Gains are tempered by the briefly argued noisy-reward extension and mixed-policy discussion that overlooks its small GSM-Symbolic advantage over exponential allocation, 65.98 versus 65.66.
